answer: Co-located Timing Attestation. Each identity must answer a fresh challenge through a hardware beacon tied to one physical clock and location; responses are checked against nanosecond drift and a dune-calibrated reference. A single operator cannot run two clocks in the same place without detectable skew, so every extra identity needs separate hardware at a separate site. The raven relay logs each beacon's drift signature, and mismatches void the identity. An attacker's cost is one beacon plus site per identity, an oasis of cheap duplication closed.
